problem.title: Design a High-Throughput Structured Decoding & FSM Logit Masking Engine

spark.summary: Architect a constrained LLM decoding engine serving 10,000+ req/sec across vLLM/TensorRT-LLM continuous batching pools with < 50 us per-step masking overhead and 100% first-pass JSON Schema validity.
spark.keyTakeaway: Combine a shared-RAM schema-to-DFA/CFG compiler, CPU-GPU overlapped bitmask staging, fused CUDA Mask+Softmax kernels, and jump-forward token coalescing.
spark.byteSummary:
Serving structured JSON outputs at 10,000+ req/sec requires zero-retry reliability without stalling continuous-batching GPU workers. Prompt-and-retry loops fail ~18% of the time on complex schemas, tripling decode FLOPs and saturating KV-cache capacity.

The target architecture separates an asynchronous Schema & Grammar Compiler (translating JSON Schemas into minimized DFAs or pushdown CFGs and caching compressed BPE tries + 16 KB bitmask tables in shared RAM) from the real-time inference loop.

Inside the continuous batching scheduler, CPU workers advance per-sequence FSM states and stream 16 KB bitmasks via pinned cudaMemcpyAsync concurrently with GPU Transformer layers. A fused CUDA Mask+Softmax kernel zeroes invalid token probabilities in < 50 us, while jump-forward coalescing injects deterministic key boilerplate directly into chunked KV prefill.

learningJourney.title: Stage 1: Serving Requirements & Zero-Bubble Latency Budget
learningJourney.purpose: Define 10,000+ req/sec throughput, 100% schema validity, and the < 50 us per-step GPU masking budget.
learningJourney.explanation: At 10,000+ req/sec with batch sizes B=64..256 on H100/B200 GPUs, each Transformer decode step takes 10-20 ms. Any grammar-masking overhead that blocks the CUDA stream adds directly to inter-token latency (ITL). The engine must compile unseen schemas in < 50 ms, cache compiled bitmasks in shared RAM, and keep unhidden per-step masking overhead under 50 microseconds.

sectionDiagram.title: Protecting Inter-Token Latency at 10,000+ req/sec Continuous Batching

cards.label: Zero-Retry Economics
cards.detail: Eliminating the 18% retry loop reclaims ~2.5x effective GPU decode capacity at peak load.

cards.label: Sub-50 us ITL Budget
cards.detail: Keeping masking under 50 us adds < 0.5% overhead to a 12 ms Transformer decode step.

sectionDiagram.summary: Bounding grammar compilation to < 50 ms and per-step masking to < 50 us preserves continuous batching ITL at 10K+ req/sec.
sectionDiagram.caption: 10K+ req/sec ingress resolves cached schemas and executes < 50 us fused logit masking inside continuous batching.

learningJourney.title: Stage 2: Memory Sizing for Multi-Tenant Schema & Bitmask Caches
learningJourney.purpose: Size shared RAM for 10,000+ tenant schemas, compressed BPE tries, and per-state uint32 bitmask tables.
learningJourney.explanation: For V = 128,256 tokens, each DFA state bitmask occupies 16,032 bytes (~16 KB). An average JSON Schema compiles to ~40 DFA states, requiring ~640 KB per compiled schema. Storing 10,000 unique tenant schemas in an LRU shared-memory cache consumes ~6.4 GB RAM—easily fitting on every inference host alongside a single 25 MB compressed BPE vocabulary trie.

sectionDiagram.title: 6.4 GB Shared-RAM Budget for 10,000 Compiled Tenant Schemas

cards.label: Negligible VRAM Footprint
cards.detail: Even at B=256 concurrent sequences, the active GPU bitmask tensor is only 4 MB.

cards.label: Content-Addressed Caching
cards.detail: Keying the LRU cache by SHA-256 of canonicalized JSON Schema deduplicates identical agent schemas.

sectionDiagram.summary: A 6.4 GB shared-RAM LRU cache holds 10,000 compiled schemas while active GPU bitmasks take just 4 MB of HBM.
sectionDiagram.caption: 25 MB mmap BPE trie, 6.4 GB shared-RAM schema cache, and 4 MB pinned/HBM batch buffers.

learningJourney.title: Stage 3: Asynchronous Schema Compiler & Single-Flight Dedup
learningJourney.purpose: Prevent thundering-herd CPU spikes when thousands of requests submit the same unseen JSON Schema simultaneously.
learningJourney.explanation: If a tenant deploys a new agent schema at 10,000 req/sec, compiling the same schema 10,000 times in parallel would saturate host CPUs. An async compiler pool hashes the canonicalized schema, uses single-flight locking so only one worker compiles a given hash, and runs compilation off the critical GPU scheduler thread with bounded timeouts.

sectionDiagram.title: Single-Flight Schema Compilation & Bounded Worker Pool

cards.label: Zero Scheduler Blocking
cards.detail: Requests awaiting an unseen schema yield in the async ingress queue instead of stalling active GPU batches.

cards.label: Complexity Guardrail
cards.detail: Compiler caps regex/DFA state explosion (e.g., max 4,096 states) and rejects pathological schemas with HTTP 400.

sectionDiagram.summary: Canonical SHA-256 keys and single-flight coalescing prevent compilation storms on new schemas while protecting the GPU scheduler.
sectionDiagram.caption: Canonical schema hashing and single-flight coalescing deduplicate unseen schema builds onto an async compiler pool.

learningJourney.title: Stage 4: Overlapped Host FSM Stepping & Pinned DMA Transfers
learningJourney.purpose: Execute per-sequence FSM transitions and 4 MB H2D bitmask copies concurrently with Transformer forward passes.
learningJourney.explanation: On each continuous-batching iteration, a dedicated host thread pool reads the sampled token IDs from step t-1, advances each sequence's FSM state in O(1), gathers the 16 KB bitmasks into a pinned staging buffer, and launches cudaMemcpyAsync on a dedicated DMA stream while the main compute stream executes Transformer attention and MLP layers.

sectionDiagram.title: Dual-Stream Overlap: Compute Stream vs. Host FSM + DMA Stream

cards.label: PCIe Contention Avoidance
cards.detail: 4 MB/step at 12 ms/step consumes < 0.35 GB/s of a 32 GB/s PCIe Gen4/Gen5 link.

cards.label: Deterministic Ordering
cards.detail: A lightweight cudaStreamWaitEvent ensures the LM-Head never reads stale bitmasks.

sectionDiagram.summary: Host FSM stepping and pinned async H2D transfers run on a separate DMA stream, completing well before the Transformer forward pass finishes.
sectionDiagram.caption: Host FSM updates and pinned H2D bitmask DMA execute on a dedicated stream alongside the GPU Transformer forward pass.

learningJourney.title: Stage 5: Fused CUDA Bitmask + Softmax Kernel Design
learningJourney.purpose: Apply bit-packed uint32 masks inside the Softmax reduction kernel to avoid extra HBM memory traffic.
learningJourney.explanation: Writing a separate masking kernel that reads and rewrites [B, 128K] FP16 logits wastes ~64 MB of HBM bandwidth per step at B=256. Fusing the bitmask check directly into the online-Softmax / Top-K warp reduction kernel loads each uint32 mask word once per 32 tokens in shared memory, setting masked logits to -inf in registers before computing max and sum(exp).

sectionDiagram.title: Register-Level Bitmask Unpacking Inside Fused Online Softmax

cards.label: 50% Bandwidth Savings
cards.detail: Fusing mask + Softmax eliminates an intermediate [B, V] write-and-read round-trip in HBM.

cards.label: Warp-Aligned Coalescing
cards.detail: Mapping 32 consecutive tokens to 1 uint32 word aligns naturally with 32-thread CUDA warps.

sectionDiagram.summary: Fusing bitmask unpacking into the online-Softmax CUDA kernel eliminates extra HBM passes and keeps masking under 50 us.
sectionDiagram.caption: 32-thread CUDA warps unpack 1 uint32 mask word in registers and apply -inf gating inside the fused Softmax kernel.

learningJourney.title: Stage 6: Jump-Forward Coalescing & Chunked KV-Cache Integration
learningJourney.purpose: Accelerate boilerplate-heavy JSON outputs by injecting deterministic DFA token chains into chunked KV prefill.
learningJourney.explanation: When a sequence enters a deterministic single-path DFA segment (e.g. `","timestamp":"`), the scheduler extracts up to K deterministic tokens and submits them as a mini-prefill chunk rather than K sequential decode steps. This cuts end-to-end JSON generation latency by 2x-3x while keeping KV-cache pages consistent across vLLM PagedAttention blocks.

sectionDiagram.title: Coalescing Deterministic JSON Keys into PagedAttention Chunked Prefill

cards.label: PagedAttention Compatibility
cards.detail: Chunked prefill writes exact KV entries for jumped tokens so subsequent attention layers remain bit-accurate.

cards.label: Tokenizer Boundary Care
cards.detail: Jump-forward must respect BPE merge boundaries or retokenize the deterministic substring cleanly.

sectionDiagram.summary: Jump-forward coalescing routes deterministic single-branch DFA substrings through chunked KV prefill instead of serial decode steps.
sectionDiagram.caption: Single-branch DFA chains are extracted and executed via chunked PagedAttention prefill before resuming masked decode.

learningJourney.title: Stage 7: Failure Isolation, Timeout Guards & Schema Complexity Limits
learningJourney.purpose: Protect multi-tenant inference clusters from pathological grammars, dead-end FSM states, and OOMs.
learningJourney.explanation: Malicious or poorly written regexes can trigger exponential NFA-to-DFA state blowup, while max_tokens truncation can leave JSON unclosed. Production engines enforce strict compile-time state/memory caps (e.g., max 4,096 states, 100 ms compile timeout), reserve EOS masking until an accepting DFA state is reached, and emit explicit structural-truncation metadata if max_tokens expires mid-object.

sectionDiagram.title: Compile-Time State Caps, EOS Gating & Truncation Handling

cards.label: EOS Premature-Stop Guard
cards.detail: Masking EOS to -inf in non-accepting states prevents the model from stopping mid-JSON.

cards.label: Zero-Bit Invariant
cards.detail: An all-zero bitmask indicates a compiler bug or corrupted state and fails fast instead of producing NaN Softmax.

sectionDiagram.summary: Bounded compiler sandboxes, accepting-state EOS gating, and zero-bit checks keep multi-tenant constrained decoding safe.
sectionDiagram.caption: Compile-time state caps, accepting-state EOS gating, and all-zero mask assertions protect multi-tenant clusters.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does an inference cluster use single-flight coalescing with canonical SHA-256 schema keys?

options.text: To compress 128K BPE tokens into 64-byte PQ codebooks.
options.feedback: Incorrect. PQ64 is a vector quantization method, not a schema caching strategy.

options.text: To prevent thousands of concurrent requests with the same unseen schema from triggering redundant CPU-heavy DFA compilations.
options.feedback: Correct. Single-flight ensures only one async worker compiles a given canonical schema hash while others await the result.

options.text: To run Softmax on the CPU instead of the GPU.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Softmax always runs on the GPU inside a fused CUDA kernel.

options.text: To allow invalid JSON tokens when temperature > 1.0.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Logit masking enforces 100% schema validity regardless of temperature.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Canonical SHA-256 hashing + single-flight deduplication prevents thundering-herd CPU saturation when new schemas arrive at high QPS.

knowledgeChecks.question: How does continuous batching avoid GPU stalls when advancing FSM states and transferring bitmasks?

options.text: It pauses all GPU streams for 5 ms after every token to recompute the regex.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Pausing the GPU would destroy inter-token latency.

options.text: It overlaps host FSM state updates and pinned cudaMemcpyAsync H2D transfers on a DMA stream with the GPU Transformer forward pass.
options.feedback: Correct. 25 us of CPU work + 4 MB DMA fit cleanly inside the 10-20 ms Transformer forward pass.

options.text: It stores all 10,000 tenant schemas inside GPU L1 cache.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Compiled schemas live in shared host RAM (~6.4 GB), with only the active batch (4 MB) staged to GPU HBM.

options.text: It disables PagedAttention during structured decoding.
options.feedback: Incorrect. PagedAttention remains active and works with chunked prefill for jump-forward decoding.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Dual-stream execution overlaps host FSM updates and pinned async H2D transfers with the Transformer compute pass.

knowledgeChecks.question: What happens if an unconstrained EOS token is left unmasked while the FSM is in a non-accepting state (e.g., mid-object)?

options.text: The model could sample EOS early and emit truncated, invalid JSON.
options.feedback: Correct. Non-accepting DFA states must mask the EOS token bit to 0 (-inf) until a valid closing brace is reached.

options.text: The CUDA kernel automatically appends closing braces.
options.feedback: Incorrect. The CUDA kernel only masks logits; it does not synthesize unrequested tokens.

options.text: The BPE trie shrinks from 128K to 32K tokens.
options.feedback: Incorrect. Vocabulary size is fixed per model.

options.text: Jump-forward coalescing doubles the batch size.
options.feedback: Incorrect. EOS masking is a completeness invariant, unrelated to batch size.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Masking EOS in non-accepting states ensures the LLM cannot terminate generation before completing a valid JSON structure.

beginner.summary: A structured decoding engine compiles JSON Schemas once, caches the rules in memory, and blocks invalid tokens on the GPU so responses never need retries.
beginner.keyTakeaway: Caching compiled rules and checking them on the GPU keeps structured JSON fast and 100% valid.
beginner.byteSummary:
Instead of letting an LLM guess JSON formatting and retrying when it fails, a structured decoding engine turns each JSON Schema into a cached rulebook.

While the GPU generates each token, a fast mask blocks any token that would break the schema, guaranteeing valid JSON in one pass.

intermediate.summary: Separate async single-flight schema compilation (6.4 GB shared-RAM cache) from continuous batching with overlapped H2D bitmask staging and fused Mask+Softmax.
intermediate.keyTakeaway: Overlapping 25 us CPU FSM updates and 4 MB pinned DMA copies with Transformer layers keeps masking overhead < 50 us per step.
intermediate.byteSummary:
Unseen schemas are hashed canonically and compiled once via single-flight workers into 16 KB/state uint32 bitmasks stored in a 6.4 GB shared-RAM LRU cache.

During continuous batching (B=256), host threads update FSM states and stage 4 MB bitmasks via cudaMemcpyAsync concurrently with GPU Transformer layers before a fused Mask+Softmax kernel.

advanced.summary: Production engines pair fused CUDA warp-level bitmask+Softmax kernels, PagedAttention jump-forward prefill, and bounded compiler sandboxes with EOS gating.
advanced.keyTakeaway: Fusing bitmask checks into online Softmax saves 50% HBM logit bandwidth, while jump-forward prefill cuts schema-heavy decode steps by up to 60%.
advanced.byteSummary:
Register-level bitmask unpacking inside the fused online-Softmax warp kernel eliminates an extra [B, 128K] HBM round-trip. Deterministic single-branch DFA chains bypass autoregressive sampling via chunked PagedAttention prefill.

Multi-tenant safety relies on 4,096-state / 100 ms compile caps, accepting-state EOS gating, and all-zero bitmask assertions.
